segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashwani and I am Anuja Kumar with the Midday News.
The headlines. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates multiple development projects worth
over 400 crore rupees at Ekthanagar in Gujarat to mark National Unity Day celebrations.

And now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid Florida tributes at the Statue of Unity in Gujarat this morning
marking Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel's 151st birth anniversary.
On the occasion, the Prime Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 31 tourism
and infrastructure projects at Ekhtha Nagar in Gujarat.
These projects are a part of continuous efforts
to expand facilities and develop the statue of unity area
as a major tourist destination.
Among the major tourist attractions inaugurated are
and IRCTC hotel built at a cost of 50 crore rupees,
the Ekhtha cruise and an eco trail.
The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones
for key infrastructural projects.
These include the Gora-Bhandara Road, Kallwani Bridge, an integrated cactus and butterfly garden and a smart zero-waste management project.
To strengthen emergency management in the region, a disaster-controlled room for the Sardar-Saroval Dam will also be constructed.
More from our correspondent.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has inaugurated multiple development projects worth over 400 crore rupees at Ektanagar, Gujarat.
to mark the national unity day celebrations today.
On the second day of his Gujarat visit, coinciding with the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar
Vallabhbhai Patel, the Prime Minister paid a solemn tribute to the Iron Man of India.
The Prime Minister offered a flora tribute at the feet of the colossal statue of unity,
while the Indian Air Force helicopters saw the flower petals over the world's tallest
statue.
Translating from the tribute to modern infrastructure, the Prime Minister flagged off a series of
green transportation initiatives boost tourism in the region. This includes two new high-tech
Vistadom buses and two eco-friendly e-buses. Further driving the vision of clean and sustainable
Ektanagar, the Prime Minister launched 20 dedicated e-waste collection vehicles and
dedicated a modern sewage treatment plant to the nation. Additionally, a new IRCTC hotel
aimed at enhancing the tourist experience was officially opened. The celebration will
We will culminate later this evening with the Grand Rastya Ekta Divas Parade at Statue

This is Chirag Ghuranya, Akashwani News, I am Dawat.
Akashwani will broadcast tonight the recording of the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture
delivered by Agriculture and Farmers' Well Feminist Shivraj Singh Johan.
The recording will be broadcast across the entire Akashwani network at 9.30pm on
On the occasion of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's birth anniversary, Agriculture and Farmers
well-feminist Shivraj Singh Chauhan said that Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's vision, determination
and leadership laid the foundation for India's national unity and territorial integrity.
He made these remarks in his address of the 67th Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture, organized
by Akashwani.
The lecture was addressed virtually by Mr. Chauhan at Aakashwani Bhavan in New Delhi.
contribution, we might never have witnessed India in the form it stands today.
His legacy will remain etched in the heart of our nation.
As a tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who served as independent India's first Deputy
Prime Minister and Information and Broadcasting Minister, Aakashwani has been organising
the annual Sardar Patel Memorial Lecture since 1955.
Over the years, this annual event has served as a rich repository of thoughts, ideas and
perspectives on a wide range of subjects.
It has also provided an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of India's diverse
cultural heritage and the various dimensions of its developmental challenges.
Union Home Minister Mit Shah has said, the vision and determination of Iron Man of India
Sardar Vallabhai Patel played a crucial role in uniting the country and establishing a strong
national identity.
He said India stands proudly on the global stage today because of the strong foundations
laid by Sardar Patel.
Mr. Shah was speaking after flagging off the run for unity at the Major Dhyan Chand
National Stadium in New Delhi this morning on the occasion of Rashtriya Ekta Divas.
Highlighting the achievements of the present government, the Home Minister said India has
made significant progress under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, including
the abrogation of Article 370 and a decisive action against nexalism.
During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's tenure, India has witnessed several historic decisions
and major achievements, such as the abrogation of Article 370, the complete integration
of Jammu and Kashmir with India, the fight against nexalism and many other significant
initiatives. However, among all these important tasks, establishing a Nasha Mukt Bharat, drug-free
India, will be one of the greatest challenges and, more importantly, one of the most significant
responsibilities for the youth of our country. It is essential for protecting the future
of our younger generation and building a stronger, healthier and more prosperous
India.
The Sehasth Kumbh Mela in Nashik and Trimbakeshwar began today at 12.02 p.m. at the auspicious
moment of Jupiter entering the Leo Zodiac.
President Robi Murmu hoisted the main flag at Ram Kundin Nashik, while Maharashtra's
Chief Minister Devendra Farnavesh hoisted the Dharm Dvaj at Kushavarth Teeth in Trimbakeshwar.

and at Ramkund.
Presidents of the Murmur will visit Trimbakeshwar in the afternoon to have a darshan and pay
obeisance to the dhvaj stump.
In the evening, the main ceremony will be held at Ramkund, where the President will
address the gathering.
President Murmur will attend the state-level Diamond Jubilee celebrations in Kurukshetra
tomorrow morning as the Chief Guest, marking the completion of 60 years since the formation
of the State of Haryana. President Rabdi Murmur will participate in various events,
including a visit to the Sri Devi Kupadrakali Temple, Gurukshetra University, and the
Gurukul, a day-come-boarding school. India has asserted that military solutions
cannot resolve global challenges, and that diplomacy must be given an opportunity
to address conflicts, speaking at the first plenary session
of the G20 Foreign Minister's meeting at Atlanta
in the United States last night.

to preserve freedom of navigation and ensure an end
to attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers
in accordance with international law,
particularly the United Nations Convention
on the Law of the Sea.
India has called on the United Nations
Human Rights Council to maintain sustained attention
terrorism, to the threat of terrorism, describing it as one of the gravest threats to human
rights, particularly the right to life.
Addressing the U.N. General Assembly in New York, first secretary at India's permanent
mission to the United Nations, Bhavika Mangalanandan said terrorism continues to pose a serious
challenge to the enjoyment of human rights.
India urged the Council to address the threat consistently, guided by the principle
of zero tolerance towards terrorism, Ms. Mangalan then also criticized the Council for politicizing
and weaponizing human rights issues and applying double standards. She cautioned that such practices
undermine the credibility of the Council. Human rights are best advanced through dialogue,
capacity building and genuine partnerships and not by politicization, selectivity or double
standards. This is critical if the Council is to speak in one voice and dispel the
the allegation of weaponization of human rights.

Islands, a key initiative announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Sixth BIMSTEC
Summit in Thailand.
The exercise, which commenced yesterday, will continue to the third of next month.

Welcome back to midday news on Aakashwani. A low pressure area remnant of Cyclonor Knob
over North Chhattisgarh and adjoining East Madhya Pradesh, South East Uttar Pradesh and
and West Jharkhand lay over southeast Uttar Pradesh and neighborhood this morning.
Meanwhile, another well-marked low-pressure area over South Andaman Sea and adjoining North
Andaman Sea and Andaman and Nicobar Islands lay over southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining
areas of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Andaman Sea this morning.
It is very likely to concentrate into a depression and intensify further and reach the west-central
Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast by Monday evening.
Meanwhile, the IMT has forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places over Arunachal Pradesh,
coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahi tomorrow.
Heavy rainfall continues to lash several parts of Orisha following the impact of the cyclonic
system with southern districts experiencing particularly intense downpours.
The Meteorological Centre has issued a yellow warning for heavy rainfall in 14
districts today. Meanwhile, the rain-related situation in Odisha remains critical, with four people
reported dead in separate incidents. A major landslide has also struck Gidipapali in Bhanjanagar,
Ganjam district, where 12 people remain missing under the debris, according to official estimates.
Search and rescue operations are underway, with personnel from Odisha Disaster Rapid Action
force and fire services working to locate those missing.
A seven-member central team led by Chitranjan Das, Joint Secretary in the Union Home Ministry,
has arrived in Andhra Pradesh to assess the damage caused by Cyclone Ornab.
According to a preliminary assessment, Cyclone Ornab has caused losses estimated at 4,764
crore rupees across 12 districts.
districts, Kona Seema and West Godavari are among the worst affected districts, meanwhile
relief and restoration operations are continuing across the affected districts.
The nation is remembering former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary today.
Congress President and Leader of Opposition in Rajasabha Malikarjun Kharge, Senior Party
Leader Sonia Gandhi and Party Leader and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi
pay tributes to Indira Gandhi at her memorial, Shakti's Thal, in New Delhi.
A tragic road accident occurred this morning around 8.30 am near Daroti village in the
Tikkar area of Shimla district, resulting in the deaths of five persons and leaving
one person injured.
The deceased include a resident of Daroti village, his mother, and three labourers
from Nepal.
On to sports. In badminton, India are assured of a place in the women's singles final at
the Heilo Open in Germany, as BB Sindhu and Anmol Karab set up all Indian semi-final clash
following impressive quarter-final victories. Sindhu cruised past Germany's Amali Schultz
in straight games, winning 21-12, 21-10. Anmol, meanwhile, put up a spirited fight
to overcome six-seed Unnati Huda in a three-game encounter.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates multiple development projects worth over 400 crore
rupees at Ek Thanagar in Gujarat to mark National Unity Day celebrations.
President Rob DeMur Muhoist's flag to mark the start of Narsik Trimbakeshwar Sihasth
Kumbh Mela in Maharashtra.
External Affairs Minister Dr. H. Jai Shankar stresses the need to preserve freedom of navigation
and ensure an end to attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers.
Relief and rescue operations underway in Udisha and Andhra Pradesh, following the impact
of Cyclone Ornab, heavy rainfall predicted over Arunachal Pradesh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh,
Kerala and Mahi tomorrow, and in Hilo open Badminton PV Sindhu to take on her compatriot
Anmol Karab in women's single semi-final clash in Germany this evening.
And with that, we end the midday news.
